summary: The appellant (Asian Hotels) challenged the Delhi High Court's order allowing the respondent-licensee to amend the plaint under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC and implead mortgagee banks under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC, challenging mortgages created by the appellant in favor of banks as void ab initio. The appellant argued that the amendment and impleadment resulted in mis-joinder of parties and causes of action, the respondent lacked locus standi, the challenge was barred by limitation and laches, and the applications were mala fide to circumvent pending arbitration under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The High Court relied on Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal and Revajeetu Builders to allow the applications. The appellant contended that the licenses were granted after the 1982 mortgages, that the license agreements recognized the right to mortgage, and that the respondents ratified these by renewing agreements. The core issue was whether a licensee could challenge pre-existing and continuing mortgages in a suit primarily concerning the licensor-licensee relationship, especially while arbitration proceedings were pending.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure
Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure
Revajeetu Builders and Developers vs. Narayanaswamy and Sons & Ors, (2009) 10 SCC 85
